title: Time: Quarter Past, Half Past, Quarter To and the Calendar
seo_title: Grade 2 Time Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Time: tell 12-hour time in hours, half hours and quarter hours on analogue clocks; use calendars to calculate and describe lengths of time in days or weeks.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 2 maths worksheets: quarter past, half past, quarter to, the calendar and time problems. 100 questions with clocks and memos.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • At quarter past, the long hand points to 3; at half past, to 6; at quarter to, to 9.
  • The short hand moves from one number to the next during the hour.
  • There are 60 minutes in an hour and 7 days in a week.
  • A calendar shows the days of each month.

Examples

Example

Long hand on 9, short hand nearly on 4

quarter to

Answer: quarter to 4

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Past or toTo: the next hour is coming.
The hour handAt quarter to 4 it is nearly on 4.
MonthsUse the calendar.

faq.a: Grade R to Grade 3 in South African schools. Learners are about 7 to 8 years old in Grade 2.
Analogue clocks to the hour, half hour and quarter hour, and calendars.

faq.q: How many minutes in a quarter of an hour?

items.e: The long hand points to the 12. The short hand points to the 1. So it is 1 o’clock. (The long hand on the 12 does not mean 12 o’clock. The short hand tells the hour.)
The long hand points to the 12. The short hand points to the 8. So it is 8 o’clock. (The long hand on the 12 does not mean 12 o’clock. The short hand tells the hour.)
The long hand points to the 12. The short hand points to the 7. So it is 7 o’clock. (The long hand on the 12 does not mean 12 o’clock. The short hand tells the hour.)
The long hand points to the 6: half way round, so it is half past. The short hand is between 1 and 2. The short hand has not reached the 2 yet, so the hour is still 1. It is half past 1.
The long hand points to the 6: half way round, so it is half past. The short hand is between 8 and 9. The short hand has not reached the 9 yet, so the hour is still 8. It is half past 8.
The long hand points to the 6: half way round, so it is half past. The short hand is between 7 and 8. The short hand has not reached the 8 yet, so the hour is still 7. It is half past 7.
The long hand points to the 3: a quarter of the way round, so it is quarter past. The short hand is between 7 and 8. The short hand has just passed the 7. It is quarter past 7.
The long hand points to the 3: a quarter of the way round, so it is quarter past. The short hand is between 8 and 9. The short hand has just passed the 8. It is quarter past 8.
The long hand points to the 3: a quarter of the way round, so it is quarter past. The short hand is between 9 and 10. The short hand has just passed the 9. It is quarter past 9.

The long hand points to the 9: a quarter of an hour before the 12, so it is quarter to. The short hand is between 10 and 11. The short hand is nearly at the 11, but not there yet. In 15 more minutes it will be 11 o’clock. So it is quarter to 11.

The long hand points to the 9: a quarter of an hour before the 12, so it is quarter to. The short hand is between 6 and 7. The short hand is nearly at the 7, but not there yet. In 15 more minutes it will be 7 o’clock. So it is quarter to 7.

The long hand points to the 9: a quarter of an hour before the 12, so it is quarter to. The short hand is between 4 and 5. The short hand is nearly at the 5, but not there yet. In 15 more minutes it will be 5 o’clock. So it is quarter to 5.

items.q: At half past, where does the long hand point?
items.e: Half past means the long hand has gone half way round the clock, from the 12 to the 6.

items.q: At quarter past, where does the long hand point?
items.e: Quarter past means the long hand has gone a quarter of the way round, from the 12 to the 3. (The 9 is for quarter to.)

items.q: At quarter to, where does the long hand point?
items.e: Quarter to means a quarter of an hour before the 12. The long hand points to the 9. (The 3 is for quarter past.)

items.q: At half past 9, where is the short hand?
items.e: In half an hour the short hand moves half way to the next number. At half past 9 it is between 9 and 10.

items.q: Quarter past 6 is how many minutes after 6 o’clock?
items.e: A quarter of an hour is 15 minutes. Count in 5s from the 12 to the 3: 5, 10, 15. (3 is the number, not the minutes.)

items.q: Quarter to 6 is how many minutes before 6 o’clock?
items.e: Quarter to 6 is a quarter of an hour before 6 o’clock. That is 15 minutes. Count in 5s back from the 12 to the 9: 5, 10, 15.

items.q: Which digital time is the same as half past 3?
items.e: Half past 3 is 30 minutes after 3 o’clock. On a digital clock it is 3:30. (Not 4:30: the hour is still 3.)

items.q: Which digital time is the same as quarter to 6?
items.e: Quarter to 6 is 15 minutes before 6 o’clock, so it is still in the 5 o’clock hour: 45 minutes past 5. That is 5:45. (6:45 is quarter to 7.)

items.q: The long hand points to the 2. How many minutes past the hour is it?
items.e: Each number on the clock is 5 minutes. Count in 5s from the 12 to the 2: 5, 10. It is 10 minutes past. (Not 2 minutes: the number is not the minutes.)

items.q: The long hand points to the 4. How many minutes past the hour is it?
items.e: Each number on the clock is 5 minutes. Count in 5s from the 12 to the 4: 5, 10, 15, 20. It is 20 minutes past. (Not 4 minutes: the number is not the minutes.)

items.q: The long hand points to the 1. How many minutes past the hour is it?
items.e: Each number on the clock is 5 minutes. Count in 5s from the 12 to the 1: 5. It is 5 minutes past. (Not 1 minute: the number is not the minutes.)

items.q: The long hand points to the 5. How many minutes past the hour is it?
items.e: Each number on the clock is 5 minutes. Count in 5s from the 12 to the 5: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. It is 25 minutes past. (Not 5 minutes: the number is not the minutes.)
The long hand points to the 2. Count in 5s from the 12: 5, 10. That is 10 minutes past. The short hand is between 4 and 5. So it is 10 past 4. The long hand is on the right-hand side, so we say past.
The long hand points to the 1. Count in 5s from the 12: 5. That is 5 minutes past. The short hand is between 3 and 4. So it is 5 past 3. The long hand is on the right-hand side, so we say past.

The long hand points to the 4. Count in 5s from the 12: 5, 10, 15, 20. That is 20 minutes past. The short hand is between 7 and 8. So it is 20 past 7. The long hand is on the right-hand side, so we say past.

The long hand points to the 5. Count in 5s from the 12: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. That is 25 minutes past. The short hand is between 10 and 11. So it is 25 past 10. The long hand is on the right-hand side, so we say past.
The long hand points to the 2. Count in 5s from the 12: 5, 10. That is 10 minutes past. The short hand is between 1 and 2. So it is 10 past 1. The long hand is on the right-hand side, so we say past.
The long hand points to the 1. Count in 5s from the 12: 5. That is 5 minutes past. The short hand is between 6 and 7. So it is 5 past 6. The long hand is on the right-hand side, so we say past.

The long hand points to the 4. Count in 5s from the 12: 5, 10, 15, 20. That is 20 minutes past. The short hand is between 5 and 6. So it is 20 past 5. The long hand is on the right-hand side, so we say past.

The long hand points to the 5. Count in 5s from the 12: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. That is 25 minutes past. The short hand is between 12 and 1. So it is 25 past 12. The long hand is on the right-hand side, so we say past.

The long hand points to the 4. Count in 5s from the 12: 5, 10, 15, 20. That is 20 minutes past. The short hand is between 3 and 4. So it is 20 past 3. The long hand is on the right-hand side, so we say past.
The long hand points to the 2. Count in 5s from the 12: 5, 10. That is 10 minutes past. The short hand is between 7 and 8. So it is 10 past 7. The long hand is on the right-hand side, so we say past.

The long hand points to the 5. Count in 5s from the 12: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. That is 25 minutes past. The short hand is between 9 and 10. So it is 25 past 9. The long hand is on the right-hand side, so we say past.
The long hand points to the 1. Count in 5s from the 12: 5. That is 5 minutes past. The short hand is between 7 and 8. So it is 5 past 7. The long hand is on the right-hand side, so we say past.

items.q: At 25 past 3, where does the long hand point?
items.e: Count in 5s from the 12 until you say 25: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. That is 5 numbers, so the long hand points to the 5. (The 7 on the other side is for 25 to.)

items.q: At 10 past 7, where does the long hand point?
items.e: Count in 5s from the 12 until you say 10: 5, 10. That is 2 numbers, so the long hand points to the 2. (The 10 on the other side is for 10 to.)

items.q: At 20 past 11, where does the long hand point?
items.e: Count in 5s from the 12 until you say 20: 5, 10, 15, 20. That is 4 numbers, so the long hand points to the 4. (The 8 on the other side is for 20 to.)

items.q: At 5 past 4, where does the long hand point?
items.e: Count in 5s from the 12 until you say 5: 5. That is 1 number, so the long hand points to the 1. (The 11 on the other side is for 5 to.)

items.q: The long hand points to the 11. How many minutes is it to the next hour?
items.e: Count in 5s back from the 11 to the 12: 5. It is 5 minutes to the hour. (55 minutes is how many minutes past.)

items.q: The long hand points to the 8. How many minutes is it to the next hour?
items.e: Count in 5s back from the 8 to the 12: 5, 10, 15, 20. It is 20 minutes to the hour. (40 minutes is how many minutes past.)

items.q: The long hand points to the 10. How many minutes is it to the next hour?
items.e: Count in 5s back from the 10 to the 12: 5, 10. It is 10 minutes to the hour. (50 minutes is how many minutes past.)

items.q: The long hand points to the 7. How many minutes is it to the next hour?
items.e: Count in 5s back from the 7 to the 12: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. It is 25 minutes to the hour. (35 minutes is how many minutes past.)

The long hand points to the 10. Count in 5s back to the 12: 5, 10. That is 10 minutes to. The short hand is between 5 and 6, nearly at the 6. So it is 10 to 6. (It is not 10 to 5: the next hour is 6.)

The long hand points to the 8. Count in 5s back to the 12: 5, 10, 15, 20. That is 20 minutes to. The short hand is between 11 and 12, nearly at the 12. So it is 20 to 12. (It is not 20 to 11: the next hour is 12.)
The long hand points to the 11. Count in 5s back to the 12: 5. That is 5 minutes to. The short hand is between 8 and 9, nearly at the 9. So it is 5 to 9. (It is not 5 to 8: the next hour is 9.)

The long hand points to the 7. Count in 5s back to the 12: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. That is 25 minutes to. The short hand is between 3 and 4, nearly at the 4. So it is 25 to 4. (It is not 25 to 3: the next hour is 4.)

The long hand points to the 10. Count in 5s back to the 12: 5, 10. That is 10 minutes to. The short hand is between 7 and 8, nearly at the 8. So it is 10 to 8. (It is not 10 to 7: the next hour is 8.)

The long hand points to the 8. Count in 5s back to the 12: 5, 10, 15, 20. That is 20 minutes to. The short hand is between 5 and 6, nearly at the 6. So it is 20 to 6. (It is not 20 to 5: the next hour is 6.)
The long hand points to the 11. Count in 5s back to the 12: 5. That is 5 minutes to. The short hand is between 5 and 6, nearly at the 6. So it is 5 to 6. (It is not 5 to 5: the next hour is 6.)

The long hand points to the 7. Count in 5s back to the 12: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. That is 25 minutes to. The short hand is between 2 and 3, nearly at the 3. So it is 25 to 3. (It is not 25 to 2: the next hour is 3.)

The long hand points to the 8. Count in 5s back to the 12: 5, 10, 15, 20. That is 20 minutes to. The short hand is between 9 and 10, nearly at the 10. So it is 20 to 10. (It is not 20 to 9: the next hour is 10.)

The long hand points to the 7. Count in 5s back to the 12: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. That is 25 minutes to. The short hand is between 8 and 9, nearly at the 9. So it is 25 to 9. (It is not 25 to 8: the next hour is 9.)

The long hand points to the 10. Count in 5s back to the 12: 5, 10. That is 10 minutes to. The short hand is between 1 and 2, nearly at the 2. So it is 10 to 2. (It is not 10 to 1: the next hour is 2.)
The long hand points to the 11. Count in 5s back to the 12: 5. That is 5 minutes to. The short hand is between 12 and 1, nearly at the 1. So it is 5 to 1. (It is not 5 to 12: the next hour is 1.)

items.q: Which digital time is the same as 25 to 9?
items.e: 25 to 9 is 25 minutes before 9 o’clock, so it is still in the 8 o’clock hour. 60 − 25 = 35 minutes past 8: 8:35. (9:35 is 35 minutes after 9 o’clock.)

items.q: Which digital time is the same as 10 to 3?
items.e: 10 to 3 is 10 minutes before 3 o’clock, so it is still in the 2 o’clock hour. 60 − 10 = 50 minutes past 2: 2:50. (3:50 is 50 minutes after 3 o’clock.)

items.q: At 10 to 4, where does the long hand point?
items.e: 10 to means 10 minutes before the 12. Count back in 5s from the 12: 5, 10. The long hand points to the 10. (The 2 is for 10 past.)

items.q: At 20 to 7, where does the long hand point?
items.e: 20 to means 20 minutes before the 12. Count back in 5s from the 12: 5, 10, 15, 20. The long hand points to the 8. (The 4 is for 20 past.)

items.q: Which month does this calendar show?
items.e: The month is at the top of the calendar: May 2 027. (Monday is a day, not a month.)

items.q: How many days are in May?
items.e: The last date is 31, so May has 31 days. (7 is the days in one row. 6 is the number of rows.)

items.q: What day of the week is 1 May?
items.e: Find 1 and go up its column to the top: Sat. 1 May is a Saturday. (A month does not always start on Monday.)

items.q: What day of the week is 12 May?
items.e: Find 12 and go up its column to the top: Wednesday.

items.q: What date comes just after 19 May?
items.e: The next date is one more: 19 + 1 = 20 May. (26 May is the date under it, one week later.)

items.q: What date comes just before 10 May?
items.e: The date before is one less: 10 − 1 = 9 May. On the calendar, 9 is at the end of the row above. (3 May is the date above 10, one week earlier.)

items.q: What day of the week is 31 May?
items.e: 31 is on its own row, in the Mon column. 31 May is a Monday.

items.q: Thandi’s birthday is circled. What is the date?
items.e: The circle is around 18. Thandi’s birthday is 18 August.

items.q: What day of the week is 20 May?
items.e: Find 20 and go up its column to the top: Thursday.

items.q: What day of the week is Thandi’s birthday?
items.e: Go up from the circled 18 to the top of its column: Wednesday.

items.q: What is the date of the first Monday in May?
items.e: Go down the Mon column. The first number is 3. So it is 3 May. (1 May is the first date, but it is a Saturday.)

items.q: Sports day is in the green box. What day of the week is it?
items.e: Go up from 6 to the top of its column: Friday. So sports day is Friday 6 August.

items.q: Which day comes after Monday?
items.e: Say the days in order: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday … So Tuesday comes after Monday. (Sunday comes before Monday.)

items.q: Which day comes before Friday?
items.e: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday. Thursday is just before Friday. (Saturday comes after Friday.)

items.q: How many days are in 1 week?
items.e: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday. That is 7 days. (5 is only the school days. 12 is the number of months.)

items.q: Which day is missing?
items.e: Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday. Wednesday is the day between Tuesday and Thursday.

items.q: Which day comes after Sunday?
items.e: Sunday is the last day on the calendar. Then a new week starts with Monday.

items.q: Which two days are the weekend?
items.e: There is no school on the weekend: Saturday and Sunday. School is Monday to Friday.

items.q: Today is Thursday. What day was it yesterday?
items.e: Yesterday is the day before. The day before Thursday is Wednesday. (Friday is tomorrow.)

items.q: How many months are in 1 year?
items.e: January to December: 12 months. (7 is the days in a week, 52 is the weeks in a year and 4 is the seasons.)

items.q: Which takes the longest?
items.e: Brushing teeth, eating an apple and putting on shoes take a few minutes. A night’s sleep takes many hours. So a night’s sleep takes the longest.

items.q: About how long does a film at the cinema last?
items.e: 2 minutes is far too short, and 2 days or 20 hours is far too long. A film lasts about 2 hours.

items.q: Which is longer: 1 hour or 45 minutes?
items.e: 1 hour is 60 minutes. 60 is more than 45. So 1 hour is longer.

items.q: Which is the shortest time?
items.e: Quarter of an hour = 15 minutes. Half an hour = 30 minutes. 1 hour = 60 minutes. 15 is the smallest, so quarter of an hour is the shortest.

items.q: Which time is the earliest?
items.e: Quarter to 8 is 15 minutes before 8 o’clock. The others are 8 o’clock or later. So quarter to 8 is the earliest.

items.q: Which time is the latest?
items.e: 25 to 5 is 4:35. 20 past 4 is 4:20 and quarter past 4 is 4:15. 4:35 is the latest, so the answer is 25 to 5.

items.q: What comes next? 3 o’clock, quarter past 3, half past 3, …
items.e: Each time is 15 minutes later. 15 minutes after half past 3 is quarter to 4.

items.q: What comes next? 5 past 2, 10 past 2, quarter past 2, …
items.e: Each time is 5 minutes later. 5 minutes after quarter past 2 (15 past) is 20 past 2.

items.q: It is 4 o’clock. What time will it be 1 hour later?
items.e: 1 hour later, the short hand moves on one number, from 4 to 5. It will be 5 o’clock.

items.q: It is half past 6. What time will it be 1 hour later?
items.e: 1 hour later, the hour goes up by 1 and the minutes stay the same. Half past 6 → half past 7.

items.q: Kabelo has tea at 5 o’clock. It is 4 o’clock now. How long until tea?
items.e: From 4 o’clock to 5 o’clock the short hand moves on one number. That is 1 hour.

items.q: Lunchtime starts at 12 o’clock and ends at half past 12. How long is lunchtime?
items.e: The long hand moves from the 12 to the 6. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. Lunchtime is 30 minutes.

items.q: Today is Wednesday 9 June. What is the date tomorrow?
items.e: Tomorrow is the next day: 9 + 1 = 10 June. (8 June was yesterday.)

items.q: Today is Wednesday 9 June. What was the date yesterday?
items.e: Yesterday is the day before: 9 − 1 = 8 June. (10 June is tomorrow.)

items.q: Today is Friday 15 October. What day of the week will it be tomorrow?
items.e: The day after Friday is Saturday. (Thursday was yesterday.)

items.q: Today is Wednesday 9 June. What day of the week will it be in 3 days?
items.e: Count on from Wednesday: Thursday (1), Friday (2), Saturday (3). It will be Saturday. (Friday counts Wednesday as day 1.)

items.q: Today is Wednesday 9 June. What is the date 1 week from today?
items.e: 1 week = 7 days. 9 + 7 = 16. Go straight down one row: 16 June. (15 June counts today as one of the 7 days.)

items.q: Today is Friday 15 October. What day of the week will it be 1 week from today?
items.e: 1 week later is 7 days later. It is always the same day of the week: Friday 22 October.

items.q: Today is Wednesday 9 June. What is the date of the next Monday?
items.e: Go forward from the box to the next date in the Mon column: 14 June. (7 June was the Monday that has gone. 13 June is a Sunday.)

items.q: Today is Wednesday 9 June. What is the date of the next Tuesday?
items.e: Go forward from the box to the next date in the Tue column: 15 June. (8 June was last Tuesday. 22 June is the Tuesday after that.)
